articles.headline: Taylor Does It Again, Victorious Secrets Hits Rock Bottom Twice
articles.deck: 63.58 points, a 53.56 point beatdown, and a second career Shart for Taylor's dumpster fire of a roster.
body: Let's start with the number because the number deserves its own eulogy. 63.58. That's what Taylor's Victorious Secrets put up in Week 6, and it is not a typo, it is not a rough week, it is a full systems failure from top to bottom of the lineup. Adam's First Down Syndrome strolled in and dropped 117.14 on him, a 53.56 point margin that isn't a loss so much as a public records request. Taylor fell to 1-6. His score was the 14th best of the week. Out of everyone. Dead last.

Let's talk about the actual humans responsible for this. Bo Nix was supposed to deliver 13.36 points and instead turned in 4.48, throwing for 107 yards on 17 of 27 with 4 carries for 2 yards, the statistical profile of a man who forgot the game was happening. Kyren Williams, the worst starter on the roster by the numbers, managed 9.7 points on 10 carries for 50 yards and 3 of 6 for 17 yards through the air, coming in at -11.17 against what he owed. Brandin Cooks caught 1 of 2 targets for 13 yards and 2.3 points. Isaiah Williams rushed once for 4 yards and 0.4 points. Terry McLaurin, a start over actual production, caught his lone target for 27 yards and all of 3.7 points, landing at -7.9 against projection. The Jacksonville Jaguars defense was projected for 8.04 and finished at negative 2 points after allowing an interception and surrendering 34 points themselves. The lone bright spot was Kyle Pitts Sr., who hauled in 5 of 7 for 60 yards and 2 touchdowns for 23 points, a healthy 15.44 over projection, but one man carrying a corpse up a hill doesn't change what's waiting at the top.

Here's the part that should really keep Taylor up at night. He benched J.K. Dobbins, who scored 13.6 points, in favor of Terry McLaurin's 3.7, a 9.9 point gift he handed back to the universe for no reason at all. Then, because apparently one unforced error wasn't enough, he benched the Cincinnati Bengals defense, who scored a modest 0, in favor of the Jacksonville Jaguars, who scored negative 2, flushing away another 2 points on a defensive swap that had no business happening. Stack those decisions next to a 53.56 point loss and you start to understand that this wasn't bad luck. This was a man building his own coffin and then personally nailing the lid.

And this isn't Taylor's first rodeo at the bottom. He sharted in Week 1 too, 63.04 points back then, and now he's got 2 Sharts to his name on the season, a club nobody wants a loyalty card for. His power ranking actually ticked up 2 spots this week, which tells you everything about how bad everyone below him is doing, because his playoff odds still sit at a bleak 0.2 percent. Victorious Secrets by name, catastrophe by nature, and at 1-6 with 9 weeks remaining, there is a lot more losing left to budget for.

So here it is, the whole wretched communion, bigger than the pitchers, bigger than the hose, bigger than the twelve pack in the parking lot, bigger even than the kiddie pool baptism, because 2 Sharts in 6 weeks means baptism isn't enough anymore, Taylor needs full immersion. Drain the actual pool. The real one, in ground, deep end and all. Empty every bottle in the house into it, every pitcher, every can with the lying cartoon animal, every last drop, and submerge him fully, face down, until the number 63.58 dissolves off his skin like it's trying to escape too. He comes up only when someone confirms in writing that his playoff odds have moved off 0.2. Chug, bitch.

articles.headline: The Hardware Week 6 Jackson Takes Home Everything But The Mantle
articles.deck: A banquet of trophies nobody asked for, handed out to men who absolutely deserve the humiliation
body: Gather round the folding table, gentlemen, because it is time to hand out hardware to a league that mostly embarrassed itself this week. Manager of the Week goes to Jackson of Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy, who dropped 130.40 points on poor Bearcat like he owed him money. This is Jackson's second time collecting this particular piece of plastic, which means somebody needs to check his lineup for performance enhancers or at minimum a functioning brain.

The Shart, lowest score of the week, belongs to Taylor of Victorious Secrets with 63.58 points. We already spent plenty of ink on that disaster elsewhere in this paper, so Taylor, go get your chug ready and we will see you in the main story.

Blowout of the week is also Jackson's, because apparently one trophy wasn't enough self esteem for the man. He buried Bearcat by 57.10 points, a margin so lopsided it should come with a concussion protocol.

Squeaker goes to Jack of Cook'd, who snuck past BedBathNBIJAN22 by the slimmest of margins, 6.14 points. Jack didn't win this game so much as fall across the finish line while BedBathNBIJAN22 tripped over his own shoelaces at the worst possible moment.

Lucky Dog is Sean of Burrowed Alive, who won with a measly 102.78 points and should be thanking whatever scheduling gods decided Matt was his opponent this week. Nothing about this win said dominance, it said survival.

Heartbreaker is Andrew of Bibi's Ballers 69, who put up 109.82 points and still lost. That is the kind of week that makes a man reconsider his waiver wire strategy, his draft strategy, and possibly his life choices in general.

Finally, Bench Rot returns to Jackson, who left 52.96 points sitting on his bench even in a week he absolutely demolished the field. Imagine scoring 130.40 and still leaving that much meat on the bone. The rest of this league should be furious, and also mildly impressed.

articles.headline: Jackson Wins Manager Of The Week, Immediately Gets Humbled By His Own Bench
articles.deck: Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy drops 130.40 on a corpse, and somehow that is still the softest Manager of the Week line all season.
body: Jackson's Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy put up 130.40 this week and ran his record to 6-1, flattening Bearcat's Hog tied and deep fried by 57.10, the biggest margin in the league this week. Bearcat came in on an L4 skid and left on one, and honestly this matchup was dead the moment the lineups locked. Jackson posted the best score in the entire league this week. He didn't just win, he won like a guy who knew the other side of the bracket forgot to show up.

The engine here was D'Andre Swift out of the flex, who went for 23 points on 16 carries for 44 yards and two rushing touchdowns plus four catches for 26 yards, beating his 15.13 projection by a wide margin. Jayden Daniels backed him up with 21 points on 29 of 40 for 300 yards and two touchdowns, clearing his 17.35 projection, and George Kittle chipped in 17.9 points on a 5 for 8, 69 yard, one touchdown day that also cleared his number. That's three starters outperforming their projections in the same lineup, which is how you get to 130.40 against a team that had no business being on the same field.

Now the part where we remember Jackson is still a degenerate who got bailed out by the schedule. He benched Tyler Shough, who put up 26.96 points, in favor of Jayden Daniels, who scored 21, leaving 5.96 points sitting on the table, and he also sat the Jets defense's 6 points for the Niners' 5, another point gone for nothing. Add it up and Jackson left 52.96 points on his own bench this week, the most in the league, and somehow still cruised. Puka Nacua caught six balls for 80 yards and still landed at 14 points against a 22.63 projection, a legit bust in a winning lineup nobody noticed because Bearcat's side of the ledger was a crime scene. And for a little perspective: Jackson's own 130.40 projected out to 138.51 before kickoff, meaning the Manager of the Week actually scored under his own number. Compare that to the other weekly highs on record this season, 169.86, 136.88, 151.64, 154.78 and 174.86, and this is the softest winning score to wear the crown all year. Enjoy the trophy, Jackson. It's heavy, but it's hollow.

articles.headline: Jack Survives A Bijan Implosion To Keep Cook'd Rolling
articles.deck: The tightest margin of the week came down to one bench decision that cost John more than the final score ever did.
body: Game of the Week honors go to the only matchup that finished inside a single score, and it delivered exactly the kind of gut punch this league exists for. Jack's Cook'd squad escaped with a 112 to 105.86 win over John's BedBathNBIJAN22, a margin of 6.14 that was the smallest of the entire week. Jack improves to 5-1 and extends his win streak to W5. John falls to 2-4 on a L3 skid that is starting to look like a pattern instead of a rough patch.

Jack did it with Michael Penix Jr. lighting up the box score at 23.1 points against a 13.62 projection, going 19 of 33 for 225 yards and 3 touchdowns despite a fumble. James Cook III matched the vibe with 24.3 points on 22 carries for 95 yards and a touchdown, adding three catches for 58 yards out of the backfield. Colston Loveland was the flex that nobody saw coming, posting 18.5 points on a 65 yard, one touchdown day against a projection of just 9.46. Not everything clicked. Nick Folk was a non factor at kicker, scoring 1 point against an 8.24 projection, but it did not matter with that much firepower around him.

John actually had the better individual story on paper. DeVonta Smith was his best starter by a mile, hauling in 7 of 14 targets for 75 yards and a touchdown for 20.5 points against an 11.9 projection. But the game turned on Bijan Robinson, who was projected for 25.16 points and delivered 7.3, a brutal 9 carries for 61 yards, 2 catches that went for negative 8 yards, nowhere close to the workhorse number John needed. That bust alone buried the upside John's 133.9 projected total promised, and he finished well under it at 105.86 while Jack cleared his 95.23 projection with room to spare.

Here is the part that will keep John up at night. He had Blake Corum sitting on his bench with 14 points, and started Bijan Robinson instead, a decision that cost him 6.7 points. The final margin was 6.14. Run that math in your head as many times as you want, the swap alone would have flipped the result. John's bench finished with 24.7 points on the sideline doing nothing while his starting running back no showed the game plan.

It was not even the worst bench call of the week, which tells you how deep the misery runs in this league right now. Over in the Burrowed Alive versus Shough Her Gently game, Matt benched Tre Tucker and his 26.7 points in favor of Tyler Allgeier's 5.8, a decision that cost him 20.9 points in a game he lost by 12.06. Matt's error was bigger in raw numbers, but Jack and John's game is the one where the bench call and the final margin lined up close enough to make every John supporter want to throw a remote. Jack's Cook'd ranked 5th in scoring this week while John's squad came in 8th, and the gap between those two numbers was exactly as thin as it felt watching it live.

articles.headline: Taylor Gets Mercy Killed While Jackson Throws A Party
articles.deck: Seven games, one certified bloodbath, and Andrew's heart in a blender yet again. Let's run it all down before the chugs get handed out.
body: Week 6 had a little bit of everything: a blowout for the ages, a nail biter that actually mattered, and Taylor quietly becoming a recurring character in this newsletter for all the wrong reasons.

Ben's Jackson Off held off Andrew's Bibi's Ballers 69, 116.72 to 109.82. Andrew put up a number that wins most weeks and still went home with nothing, which at this point should just be his walkout music.

Josef's Zyn-bo Squisher turned Trip's 50 Shades of Zay into a cautionary tale, 121.38 to 94.78, with Christian McCaffrey dropping 30.7 and Malik Nabers chipping in 28.5. That's not a fantasy matchup, that's a mugging with a receipt.

Sean's Burrowed Alive beat Matt's Shough Her Gently 102.78 to 90.72, and yes, 102.78 was enough to win this week, which tells you everything about the state of Shough Her Gently. Matt's sitting at 1-5 and the 0.7 playoff odds say the fat lady isn't singing, she's already in the parking lot.

Adam's First Down Syndrome absolutely ran Taylor's Victorious Secrets off the field, 117.14 to 63.58, a 53.56 point massacre fueled by Germie Bernard's 25.7 and Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 25.4. Taylor takes home The Shart again, his second trip to the podium this season, and at this rate the league should just name a chug after him.

Jack's Cook'd needed every last point to hold off John's BedBathNBIJAN22, 112 to 105.86, your Squeaker and Game of the Week rolled into one gorgeous 6.14 point margin. This is what a real fantasy football game is supposed to feel like, and the rest of you should take notes.

And then there's Jackson. Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy put a combine on Bearcat's Hog tied and deep fried, 130.4 to 73.3, a 57.1 point beatdown that was the Blowout of the week before Bhayshul Tuten's 24.7 even had a chance to matter for Bearcat. Didn't help. Nothing was helping.
Aaron's Romo911 closed out the slate with a 107.6 to 95.02 win over Jeff's Chase Browns with Downs, keeping the Bubble crowded and everyone's blood pressure elevated heading into next week.

articles.headline: Adam And Bearcat Dig Gold Out Of The Waiver Dumpster
articles.deck: While Jackson was off whipping 130.40 on everyone, a couple of desperate degenerates found their saviors on the wire and actually used them right.
body: Adam's First Down Syndrome squad sits at 3-3, clawing for playoff oxygen at 56.4 percent to make it, and this week he leaned on two names that smell like waiver wire miracles. Germie Bernard went off for 25.7 and Jaxon Smith-Njigba added 25.4, and together that duo carried Adam to a 117.14 beatdown of poor Taylor, who put up a league worst 63.58 and will forever be remembered as this week's Shart. Adam didn't need to explain himself. The box score did it for him.

Meanwhile Bearcat is drowning at 1-5 with a 1.3 percent shot at the playoffs, the kind of record where you start taking wild swings just to feel something. He found one. Bhayshul Tuten dropped 24.7 points in a losing effort against Jackson's 130.40 juggernaut, which still ended in a 57.10 point blowout loss, but credit where it's due, Bearcat picked a live body in a dead season. That's the energy you want from a guy with nothing to lose. Keep digging, Bearcat, there's gotta be a live one buried under all that dirt somewhere.

Two guys at the bottom of the standings found real production this week. Doesn't fix the record. Does prove they're paying attention, which honestly might be more than we can say for some of the teams ahead of them.

articles.headline: Big Performances: Josef Doubles Up While Trip Torches His Own Bench
articles.deck: Six guys went off this week. Only some of their managers were smart enough to notice before kickoff.
body: Josef had the best fantasy day anybody had all week and split it between two guys on the same roster. Christian McCaffrey went for 16 CAR, 64 YD, 2 RUSH TD, 9/10 REC, 53 YD, 1 FUM, good for 30.7 against a projection of 20.56, a plus 10.14 beatdown of Vegas math. Then Malik Nabers casually dropped 12/15 REC, 165 YD for 28.5 points on a 14.94 projection, a plus 13.56 that should be illegal in a league this size. Zyn-bo Squisher rolled in at 4-2 on a W1 streak and buried 50 Shades of Zay 121.38 to 94.78, a 26.6 margin that was never in doubt.

Which brings us to Trip, who had the single best individual stat line of anyone not named McCaffrey or Nabers and still lost. Kenneth Walker III went 19 CAR, 128 YD, 2 RUSH TD, 2/3 REC, 11 YD for 27.9 points on a 22.76 projection, a plus 5.14 night. Didn't matter. Trip benched Trevor Lawrence, who put up 27.34 points, in favor of Matthew Stafford's 16.88, a 10.46 point gift he handed to Josef for free. Then he doubled down and sat Emmett Johnson's 4.4 points for Juwan Johnson's zero, another 4.4 down the drain. Harold Fannin Jr. finished with 1.9 on an 11.18 projection too, just to make sure nothing worked. Trip entered the week 4-2 on an L2 skid, and out of all 14 teams in this league, his final score landed dead last among winners who actually tried.

Adam ran the same two-star trick on First Down Syndrome. Germie Bernard caught 11/12 REC, 87 YD, 1 REC TD for 25.7 on a 9.96 projection, a plus 15.74 explosion, while Jaxon Smith-Njigba added 12/16 REC, 134 YD for 25.4 against a 22.5 projection. First Down Syndrome demolished Victorious Secrets 117.14 to 63.58, a 53.56 margin, entering the week 3-3 on a W2 run.

And then there's Bearcat, who got a legitimately great game from Bhayshul Tuten, 12 CAR, 39 YD, 4/4 REC, 48 YD, 2 REC TD for 24.7 on a 13.19 projection, and it still bought him nothing. Hog tied and deep fried lost to Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy 73.3 to 130.4, a 57.1 margin, dropping Bearcat to 1-5 on an L4 streak that Tuten alone could not fix.

articles.headline: Power Rankings: Jackson Rules The Roost, Matt Finds The Basement
articles.deck: Week 6 in the books, 9 weeks left, 7 playoff spots, and most of this league is already running on fumes and bad decisions.
body: Fourteen teams, one trophy case, and a whole lot of bubble teams lying to themselves about their playoff odds. Here's where everybody stands after Week 6.

1. Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy (Jackson): Dropped 130.40 on Bearcat by 57.10, grabbed Manager of the Week, and still left 52.96 points rotting on the bench. Clinch Watch at 97.2%, start printing the bye week shirts.
2. Cook'd (Jack): Survived a 6.14 point nail-biter over John's BedBathNBIJAN22 in the Game of the Week. Winning ugly works just as well as winning pretty when you're sitting at 86.5%.
3. Jackson Off (Ben): Put up 116.72 to edge Andrew's Bibi's Ballers. Sitting at 84.7% playoff odds while pretending he's not sweating the bubble like everyone else.
4. Romo911 (Aaron): Beat Chase Browns with Downs 107.60 to 95.02, but Aaron's got two Shart trophies sitting in his case like a bad tattoo he can't laser off.
5. 50 Shades of Zay (Trip): Got run over by 26.6 points despite Kenneth Walker III going off for 27.9. Trip's defense watched that one from the parking lot.
6. Chase Browns with Downs (Jeff): Dropped 95.02 in the loss, but 72% playoff odds mean Jeff can afford one more bad Tuesday night.

7. First Down Syndrome (Adam): Moved up a spot torching Victorious Secrets 117.14 to 63.58. Germie Bernard and Jaxon Smith-Njigba combined for a stupid amount of production while Adam crawls out of mediocrity.
8. Zyn-bo Squisher (Josef): Somehow dropped a spot despite Christian McCaffrey putting up 30.7 and Malik Nabers adding 28.5. Tells you everything about how deep this league actually is.
9. Bibi's Ballers 69 (Andrew): Scored 109.82 and still lost, taking home the Heartbreaker trophy and a 43.3% coin flip at the playoffs.
10. BedBathNBIJAN22 (John): Put up 105.86 in a loss that's going to haunt John's group chat all week. Sitting at 43.7% to sneak in.
11. Burrowed Alive (Sean): Won with just 102.78, the Lucky Dog of the week. At 10.5% playoff odds, that luck needs to show up a few more times.
12. Hog tied and deep fried (Bearcat): Got smoked 73.30 to 130.40, though Bhayshul Tuten's 24.7 was the one bright spot in an otherwise 1.3% future.

13. Victorious Secrets (Taylor): Posted 63.58, claimed the Shart for the second time, and somehow moved up a spot anyway. The fantasy equivalent of getting promoted after fainting during the presentation.
14. Shough Her Gently (Matt): Fell to Burrowed Alive's lowly 102.78, dropped to dead last, and Matt's 0.7% playoff odds are basically a hospice sentence at this point.

articles.headline: The Trade Desk Is Open And Everyone Stayed Home
articles.deck: Zero trades got done in Week 6, so instead we are grading the real deals that got made at the worst possible time: starting lineups.
body: Let the record show the Squirtnite FFL trade desk processed exactly nothing this week. No picks moved, no bye week panic deals, not even a courtesy throw-in. While you all sat on your hands, your benches were out here making trades for you, and most of you lost the deal.

Andrew traded Bryce Young for Aaron Rodgers before the games even started and it cost him 3.82 points. Rodgers went 16.02, Young sat there with 19.84, and Bibi's Ballers 69 lost by 6.9 with 109.82 on the board, the single highest losing score of the week. Grade: F for the swap, A for the heartbreak tour.

Trip somehow benched Trevor Lawrence's 27.34 to start Matthew Stafford's 16.88, a 10.46 point self-inflicted wound, and 50 Shades of Zay got run off the field by 26.6 anyway with a week rank of 11. That is not a trade, that is a hostage situation.

Two men cost themselves the whole game. Matt sat Tre Tucker's 26.7 for Tyler Allgeier's 5.8, a 20.9 point gift to Burrowed Alive in a 12.06 point loss, textbook benched the win. John did the same thing smaller, parking Blake Corum's 14 for Bijan Robinson's 7.3, a 6.7 point cost in a 6.14 point loss to Cook'd. Every trade on the books this week gets an Incomplete, because the only transactions anyone made were with their own Sunday morning lineup, and the house always wins.

articles.headline: Jackson Hosts a Mercy Killing, Taylor Volunteers as Tribute
articles.deck: The league's best team gets fed the league's worst team, and somewhere a chug is already being poured preemptively
body: Nunnells sits at 97.2 percent to make the playoffs, just dropped a 130.40 on the field, and now gets to host Victorious Secrets, who have lost five straight and are clinging to a 0.5 percent playoff chance like a toddler clinging to a steak knife. Taylor already owns two Shart trophies this season. There is no version of this preview where I pretend that trend stops here. This is your Shart Bowl, ladies and gentlemen, and the betting line isn't close.

Elsewhere the actual football is pretty good. Jack's Cook'd squad, sitting at 5-1 with an 86.5 percent playoff clip, hosts Aaron's Romo911 crew in a matchup of two teams that both know how to win ugly and win close. Ben's Jackson Off travels to face Josef's Zyn-bo Squisher, a borderline-playoff clash between a team that just mashed the Ballers and a team still riding Christian McCaffrey's 30.70 from last week. Trip's 50 Shades of Zay heads into First Down Syndrome looking to keep pace in a crowded bubble that has basically everyone from seed 3 through seed 10 sweating.

Then there's Bearcat, 1-5 with a 1.3 percent playoff shot, hosting Jeff's Chase Browns with Downs. If Taylor somehow finds a way to avoid the gutter, Bearcat is standing right behind him with a towel.

body: No stat corrections changed a published result this week.
